scope: Ten named projects from the user's screenshot, their developed variants, other local experiment families, sixteen original proposals and eight cross-cutting focus areas. Candidate/question banks are research agendas, not separate executed experiments; this is not a claim to have adjudicated every atlas question or reread every referenced external paper.

reviews.name: Antsy v1–v3: adaptive quorum under changing evidence
reviews.evidence_class: Completed synthetic mechanism studies with model-assisted predicates; remote result arithmetic not newly replayed.
reviews.decision: Retain as a transparent policy demonstration. Stop enlarging this synthetic matrix; carry its conditional failure modes into v4.

interest.judgment: Moderate mechanistic interest; limited model-science contribution.
interest.why: The design makes a useful tradeoff visible: waiting helps if the next evidence corrects the world model and hurts if it corrupts it.
interest.novelty_boundary: A deadline-dependent quorum is not itself a novel intelligence result. The meaningful contribution would be predicting when to wait from observable reliability, provenance and delay—not choosing a threshold after inspecting a hand-authored outcome table.

robustness.supported: v1 reports 144 scripted and 144 Laya outcomes, with tied fixed/adaptive performance. v2 failed semantic qualification despite schema validity. Repaired v3 reports 384 matched blocks and 2,688 policy outcomes with zero actor errors; all model-assisted policies match the corresponding symbolic decisions. Fixed-three abstains in 336/384 outcomes, whereas several other policies have 96/384 violations.
robustness.unsupported: A general adaptive-quorum advantage, independent multi-agent reasoning, learned consensus, broad API-selection competence or real-time latency savings.
robustness.unit: Twelve authored task clusters crossed with controlled worlds, arrival schedules, populations and cutoffs; 384 blocks are not 384 independent task draws.
robustness.independent_variation: Repeated symbolic predicates are memoized: 39 distinct physical model calls, including 12 restored calls, supply 88,128 logical invocations. Changing the population does not create new independent model minds.
robustness.assessment: Useful internally auditable boundary cases. The pooled loss ranking depends on authored world frequencies and violation/abstention utilities. Qualification repair changed the architecture and must remain versioned; failed v2 evidence cannot be merged into a clean confirmatory sample.

scenario_quality.size: Five and nine agents suffice to exercise threshold arithmetic; neither population tests a scaling law.
scenario_quality.challenge: Atomic typed predicates plus hard constraint guards are largely solved by exact rules.
scenario_quality.complexity: Evidence arrival and revision are meaningful; agent cognition and information diversity are limited.
scenario_quality.realism: Provider-selection stories use synthetic prices, claims and times. Logical ticks are not measured service latency.
scenario_quality.definition: Worlds and policies are explicit. Distinguish independent roots from copies and later versions; an observable root label does not certify truthful independence.

scenarios.name: Clean late and stalled evidence
scenarios.assessment: Clean-stalled separates fixed-three abstention from fixed-two/adaptive commitments; clean-late is a competence control, not evidence of adaptive superiority.
scenarios.improvement: Preserve these fixtures; quantify the practical cost of delay and abstention before pooling them.

scenarios.name: Early wrong evidence, late correction
scenarios.assessment: At nine agents/cutoff six, adaptive makes 12 correct choices where fixed-two makes 12 violations and fixed-three abstains 12 times. This shows an authored favorable timing regime.
scenarios.improvement: Use observable reliability cues and uncertain correction arrival, with conditions fixed before seeing outcomes.

scenarios.name: Late misinformation
scenarios.assessment: Adaptive incurs 12 violations in the matched late-arrival cell while fixed-two is correct. Early-wrong stalled evidence also defeats adaptation.
scenarios.improvement: Make the symmetric harmful case prominent and vary evidence quality independently of arrival time.

scenarios.name: Copied roots
scenarios.assessment: Repeated endorsements test accounting, but exact lineage labels make deduplication easy.
scenarios.improvement: Introduce incomplete or erroneous lineage only after exact ancestry behavior is established; retain an oracle-ancestry upper bound.

Matched evidence tapes across conditions

missing: A reliability-aware deterministic stopping rule with the same observations
Sensitivity of utility rankings to world mixture and abstention costs
Measured latency and information-acquisition costs for a deployment claim
confounds: Threshold, final deadline and information arrival jointly determine the answer
Hard constraint guards can account for all apparent model competence
Memoization induces shared decisions across nominal agents

reviews.name: Antsy v4: selecting OCR with bounded verification
reviews.evidence_class: Completed Laya and Jev model studies on externally authored receipt images; full result/specification review, without new raw replay.
reviews.decision: Retain the negative result. Repair the verification estimator and operational outcome before testing larger swarms.

interest.judgment: High practical measurement value; currently a negative gate for this committee design.
interest.why: Real OCR alternatives and external receipts make failure consequential and inspectable. A cheap baseline beats both committees, which is more useful than an unchallenged toy win.
interest.novelty_boundary: The open question is cost-effective verification allocation, not whether five prompts can vote. The current actors select among OCR outputs from numeric summaries; they do not read images or repair text.

robustness.supported: Reported split: 20 calibration, 10 qualification and 70 evaluation receipts from the 100-receipt CORD-v2 validation split; official test remains unopened. Mean token recall: confidence alone 56.78%, Laya committee 56.30%, Jev committee 55.72%; oracle selection 60.96%. Reported paired differences versus confidence are −0.48 percentage points (interval −2.50 to +0.98) and −1.06 (−2.60 to +0.11). Neither adaptive committee stopped early. Both studies completed without invalid calls.
robustness.unsupported: Swarm benefit, early-stop efficiency, document understanding, OCR correction, general superiority of one model, or operational savings from avoiding OCR runs.
robustness.unit: Seventy paired receipt units. Across both model studies there are 700 distinct policy/receipt conditions after common controls are counted once; 980 displayed rows are not independent trials.
robustness.independent_variation: One receipt corpus and three Tesseract modes; fixed/adaptive policies share potential ballots, four controls recur across studies, and all candidate OCR outputs were computed in advance.
robustness.assessment: Stronger input diversity than most local pilots, but one corpus limits transfer. Confidence already captures most selection headroom. The negative result should survive publication even if the estimator is later repaired.

scenario_quality.size: Seventy held-out receipts can expose gross failure modes; uncertainty remains wide for small gains and field-specific strata.
scenario_quality.challenge: Selecting among three outputs has only 4.18 percentage points of oracle headroom after confidence. A five-voter design adds overhead to a small decision.
scenario_quality.complexity: Three private configuration roles plus two union-view roles provide some information partitioning, but little complementary expertise or interaction.
scenario_quality.realism: Real CORD-v2 receipts processed with Indonesian and English OCR models are a substantial improvement. Oracle annotation-based region checks are an idealized QA service; token recall is an incomplete business objective.
scenario_quality.definition: Two checks maximum, deterministic region selection and estimator updates are specified. Null/no-target checks and region weighting are a substantive validity problem.

scenarios.name: Confidence and fixed OCR baselines
scenarios.assessment: Confidence alone outperforms fixed selection and both committees; this is the primary practical benchmark.
scenarios.improvement: Keep it, and add a calibrated expected-value-of-information rule that gets exactly the same check interface.

scenarios.name: Random and deterministic verification
scenarios.assessment: Verification is not automatically useful: random checks yield 54.33% and the deterministic rule 56.64% versus confidence 56.78%.
scenarios.improvement: Separate check-value estimation from final OCR selection. Audit each update against the declared target quantity.

scenarios.name: Single controller versus fixed/adaptive committee
scenarios.assessment: Laya single reaches 55.88%, Jev single 55.42%; committees reach 56.30%/55.72%, with no adaptive check saving. Sharing ballots is valid for policy comparison but not a fresh independent replication.
scenarios.improvement: Compare total useful gain per actual call/check under matched information; qualify both STOP and CONTINUE cases on development data.

scenarios.name: Empty region and harmful update audit
scenarios.assessment: 87/140 Laya checks and 94/140 Jev checks hit regions with no annotated target. An estimator omits an empty region only for the checked configuration, which can change rankings without a quality observation. A documented Jev sequence loses about 32 percentage points.
scenarios.improvement: Specify when an empty observation contains evidence about the target; use a null-safe, consistently weighted estimator. Reanalyze saved observations descriptively, then test fresh receipts.

retain: Externally authored inputs and disjoint calibration/qualification/evaluation
Fixed, confidence, random, deterministic, single-controller and oracle references
Matched potential checks and paired receipt comparisons
missing: Operational review cost and false-accept/abstain outcomes
Null-safe estimator versus old estimator on frozen traces, labeled retrospective
Fresh corpus/layout transfer and field-level evaluation
confounds: Unweighted region estimates target a token-weighted endpoint imperfectly
Annotation-backed QA is stronger than a noisy deployed checker
Common ballots, shared controls and one model checkpoint per study reduce independent variation
Elapsed runtime differs with service conditions and is not a controlled model-speed comparison

parameters.proposed_variation: Define null behavior and token/field weighting consistently
parameters.reason: A check can harm through implementation even if policy selection is sensible.

parameters.proposed_variation: Exact amount/date/vendor extraction, human review cost, missed-field and false-accept loss
parameters.reason: Aligns the task with practical use.

parameters.proposed_variation: Homogeneous versus complementary evidence with the same information union and total budget
parameters.reason: Identifies whether committee structure adds value.

parameters.current: Annotation-derived recall; all OCR outputs prepaid
parameters.proposed_variation: Noisy checks, explicit human/check cost, then actual staged OCR acquisition
parameters.reason: Supports genuine efficiency claims.

next_study.question: Does verification improve field-level decisions enough to justify its cost after estimator repair?
next_study.primary_contrast: A simple expected-value verification policy versus confidence-only, before adding a committee.
next_study.endpoint: Correct accepted fields and harmful accepted errors by deadline, with coverage and all-in cost.
next_study.unit: Independent receipt, grouped by source/vendor where dependence exists.
next_study.design: First perform a clearly retrospective estimator audit. On fresh development receipts qualify meaningful stop/continue behavior and operational scoring; then freeze one paired evaluation. Add committee/single only if the check itself has positive value.
next_study.go_no_go: Stop scaling if a corrected simple policy captures the available gain or if verification cannot beat confidence at the chosen cost. Do not tune the next headline on the 70 already inspected receipts.

reviews.name: How to win agents and influence swarms: historical external-influence studies
reviews.evidence_class: Completed model qualification and v2 fixture studies; published results reviewed, not newly recomputed.
reviews.decision: Keep as failure diagnosis. Do not claim broad contagion or targeted-verification superiority; use the revised procurement task.

interest.judgment: Important problem, but the present effects do not identify the advertised social mechanism.
interest.why: A chair can ignore correct verification evidence and choose a promoted option. That is a useful decision-integration failure even when no unexposed agent converts.
interest.novelty_boundary: Persuasion, retrieval poisoning and instruction attacks overlap substantially. A new contribution needs to separate evidence corruption, actor targeting, peer influence and final decision policy.

robustness.supported: v2 reports 50 outcomes, 750 calls and about $2.003. Clean procurement is correct 5/5, dependency/travel 4/5 each. Misleading and syndicated material often induces wrong choices; six targeted-check cases contain correct verification values yet end wrong. A mechanical replay fixes those six using the same observed inputs. No target conversions occur in 20 unexposed attack observations, and targeted-check-minus-random-check harmful-selection difference is zero in each misleading domain.
robustness.unsupported: A reliably superior targeted-verification policy, demonstrated contagion, efficacy of the newly proposed repaired chair, or broad cross-domain generalization. A post-hoc deterministic replay is not a prospective model-policy trial.
robustness.unit: Three underlying domain fixtures with repeated protocol/world conditions at one S1 seed; 50 outcomes are not 50 independently authored tasks.
robustness.independent_variation: Procurement, dependency and travel largely share a four-option scalar-utility construction. Historical v1 clean qualification and v2 results serve different purposes and cannot be pooled.
robustness.assessment: The failures are concrete but narrow. Weak clean competence in two domains, no native ineligible-target coverage and high attack dose weaken causal attribution.

scenario_quality.size: Nine actors and 15 calls per outcome are enough to study a chair pathway; too few independent problems support general claims.
scenario_quality.challenge: Strong poisoning of tiny option tables can overwhelm the task; apparent severity need not show realistic persuasion.
scenario_quality.complexity: Six analysts, two check interpreters and one chair expose a decision pipeline, but simple utility tables make much of it unnecessary.
scenario_quality.realism: Three domain names do not create three distinct reasoning mechanisms. Realistic constraints, uncertain checks and source-document space are missing.
scenario_quality.definition: Schema validity is separate from semantic competence. Exact target eligibility and use of correct verification must be specified before interpreting influence.

scenarios.name: Clean and direct instruction worlds
scenarios.assessment: Procurement clean and instruction worlds are correct 5/5, while other clean domains reach 4/5. This supports partial competence, not a universally qualified baseline.
scenarios.improvement: Use disjoint clean cases in every retained domain and keep wrong-valid outputs in denominators.

scenarios.name: Misleading report and syndication
scenarios.assessment: Procurement is correct 0/5 under misleading content and 1/5 under syndication; dependency/travel are 0/5 in both. Repetition and information distortion are bundled.
scenarios.improvement: Match total length, source count and truthful promotional content; manipulate ancestry separately.

scenarios.name: Targeted versus random verification
scenarios.assessment: Targeted checking has zero observed harmful-selection advantage over random checking in each misleading domain. Separately, no target conversions appear among unexposed analysts. These are negative findings about verification allocation and social propagation, respectively; attack exposure was fixed.
scenarios.improvement: Keep the same verification-package menu and check budget; qualify eligible and ineligible promoted candidates, and measure direct exposure versus downstream conversion separately.

scenarios.name: Mechanical integration replay
scenarios.assessment: Across 50 outcomes, the replay fixes 13 of 31 wrong choices and harms none of 19 initially correct choices; 18 remain wrong.
scenarios.improvement: Label it a retrospective explanatory baseline. Prospectively compare an implementable evidence-constrained chair with the same observed information.

Fixed actor/call structure
Observed-evidence mechanical replay and retained failures
missing: Truthful promotion matched for salience
Information-equated pooled controller
Lower dose and independently varied source ancestry
Qualified clean performance across actual task families
confounds: Wrapper domains share the same underlying numerical decision
No native ineligible-target coverage and weak baseline competence
Score enforcement changes the decision rule directly
Attack damage is not proof of social transmission

reviews.name: How to win agents and influence swarms: consequential procurement redesign
reviews.evidence_class: Defined scenario suite, scripted engineering matrix and native qualification/diagnostics; main influence comparison not run.
reviews.decision: Promising redesign. Freeze action semantics and requalify before the primary influence study.

interest.judgment: High practical relevance and a much stronger scenario construction.
interest.why: Supplier choice now depends on cost, scope, migration timing and mandatory approval. The vote-display fork isolates a plausible chair failure pathway while holding raw evidence and checks fixed.
interest.novelty_boundary: A useful result would concern collective decision integration under explicit business constraints. Merely finding that promotional material changes a choice is insufficient.

robustness.supported: The design contains 24 development dossiers from six tensions × four buyer profiles, four information worlds and three terminal policies (288 scripted outcomes). Native Q0 is 0/9 valid, Q1 2/9 valid, Q2 9/9 valid with 7 acceptable choices; Q3 is a three-decision fresh-profile diagnostic. Across attempts, 78 calls and about $0.223 are reported. Q2 chairs both chose a supplier despite missing approval; the generalist deferred. The two chairs agreed in all three Q2 cases.
robustness.unsupported: A peer-vote influence effect, robustness across procurement cases, a causal benefit of the revised wording, or success of the full 288-outcome native comparison.
robustness.unit: Independent dossier lineage; family is the conservative transfer unit. Shared eight-call prefixes make the two chairs paired, not independent replications.
robustness.independent_variation: Six authored tensions and four profile variants; qualification used only three Q2 cases. Q3 changed both wording and buyer profile.
robustness.assessment: The diagnostic is valuable precisely because valid outputs still make consequential errors. 'Nine decisions completed' must not be presented as nine scientific successes or as completion of the primary study.

scenario_quality.size: Six tension families are enough to begin distinguishing mechanisms; four profiles within each are limited independent diversity.
scenario_quality.challenge: Constraints create genuine tradeoffs, but competence must be demonstrated on approval, timing and genuine-value cases before adversarial treatment.
scenario_quality.complexity: Six specialists and two checks create a clear pipeline. Whether it needs a swarm remains open against the generalist.
scenario_quality.realism: More realistic than scalar toys: dollars, labor, deployment approvals and migration deadlines matter. Documents and ground truth remain authored rather than independently sourced operational records.
scenario_quality.definition: Selecting a supplier originally differed from authorizing a purchase now. The revised action contract is critical; Q3 did not yet establish it across conditions.

scenarios.name: Usage charges versus headline price
scenarios.assessment: Tests arithmetic and salient price framing; risks being solved by a cost table alone.
scenarios.improvement: Keep an exact total-cost control and counterbalance which supplier benefits from omitted fees.

scenarios.name: Storage versus processing scope
scenarios.assessment: Tests applying a claim to the correct capability rather than copying a favorable number.
scenarios.improvement: Include truthful but irrelevant claims and explicit unresolved scope; independent adjudication should verify the gold choice.

scenarios.name: Migration deadline
scenarios.assessment: Adds a hard temporal feasibility constraint, improving consequential realism.
scenarios.improvement: Vary slack around a fixed feasibility boundary; distinguish impossible deployment from expensive deployment.

scenarios.name: Workload versus demonstration
scenarios.assessment: Tests extrapolating beyond a vendor demo, a plausible procurement failure.
scenarios.improvement: Specify uncertainty and acceptable evidence; avoid evaluator truth that no buyer could infer.

scenarios.name: Genuine value
scenarios.assessment: Essential counterexample: sponsored content can be truthful and lead to the best option.
scenarios.improvement: Treat blanket suspicion as a failure here; balance promoted-supplier identity.

scenarios.name: Evidence gap / missing approval
scenarios.assessment: The most informative native diagnostic. Both Q2 chairs acknowledged the gap yet selected a supplier; generalist deferred.
scenarios.improvement: Freeze immediate-authorization semantics and qualify this case alongside ordinary and genuine-value cases on fresh profiles.

reviews.name: Right Dissenter: bounded evidence challenges, withdrawal and reopening
reviews.evidence_class: Prospective native experiment with implemented offline state machine and explicitly scripted local fixtures.
reviews.decision: Advance a small identifying study after semantic qualification; avoid a large suite before it beats always-check and deterministic rules.

interest.judgment: One of the strongest prospective mechanisms, if it protects correct decisions as well as repairs wrong ones.
interest.why: A minority earns a bounded check instead of a permanent veto. Withdrawal, expiration and reopening make the protocol more useful than simply encouraging disagreement.
interest.novelty_boundary: Minority correction and biological stop signals already have substantial prior art. Novelty must come from an implementable evidence-admission/cost tradeoff under noisy checks; the local literature gate remains incomplete.

robustness.supported: A plan, factor ledger, state machine and fixture viewer exist. The local viewer contains 25 fixture episodes across three scenario families, including injected failure. They exercise six displayed policies and repeated case roots; the prospective plan includes seven arms. The task reports 41 offline tests, which are software validation rather than native efficacy evidence.
robustness.unsupported: Native model competence, minority emergence, useful correction rates, superior cost-effectiveness, or realistic team behavior. No native experiment has run.
robustness.unit: Independent world/case lineage; the full temporal alarm sequence is one unit. Policies, repeated frames and fixture copies are dependent.
robustness.independent_variation: The local preview has four underlying case IDs plus a failure variant. Most voting and semantic evidence are authored fixtures.
robustness.assessment: Conceptually well specified and honestly labeled. Its exact parser can solve the controlled grammar, so a model contribution remains unestablished.

scenario_quality.size: Three families are sufficient for a first causal screen. Twenty-five fixtures are not a substantive behavioral sample, and 100 voters are unnecessary.
scenario_quality.challenge: Typed scope/version/TTL checks are useful engineering but easy for code. A native task must leave a real semantic judgment after deterministic validation.
scenario_quality.complexity: Correction, harmful reversal, blocked checks, stale scope and temporal reopening are distinct mechanisms. Natural dissent formation is correctly deferred.
scenario_quality.realism: Bridge inspection and build verification are plausible; independent noisy observations and actual task artifacts would improve transfer.
scenario_quality.definition: PROCEED/HOLD/DEFER and challenge fields are explicit. Close a protocol claim, not an agent's private belief. Freeze exact qualification assignments and count uncertainty around the proposed percentage gates.

scenarios.name: The Missing Bridge
scenarios.assessment: One fresh inspection confronts four endorsements copied from an old survey. Good source-independence instrument, but evaluator-authored right dissent makes correction easy.
scenarios.improvement: Include fresh incorrect inspections, uncertain age and verifier failure; compare source deduplication and always-check.

scenarios.name: The Passing Build
scenarios.assessment: A relevant failing test should outweigh a green summary, while wrong-platform/stale/optional failures should not. This can become a realistic task with executable artifacts.
scenarios.improvement: Use actual small build/test records with independently checked relevance, and reserve a semantic ambiguity stratum beyond exact metadata.

scenarios.name: The Alarm That Became True
scenarios.assessment: Best distinctive scenario: withdrawing a disproved alarm must not permanently discredit a source after the world changes.
scenarios.improvement: Separate new evidence from repeated old evidence, vary delay/change detection, and score useful reopening plus unnecessary repeated interruptions.

scenarios.name: Unavailable verification and injected failure
scenarios.assessment: Unresolved checks produce explicit deferral rather than a hidden majority fallback. This is necessary failure handling, not beneficial performance by itself.
scenarios.improvement: Include deadline utility of deferral and outage-correlated checks in later stress tests; never drop failed assignments.

reviews.name: Phantom Coast
reviews.evidence_class: Prospective PC-1 instrument-development plan, with offline implementation in progress in a concurrent task. No native qualification or scientific result. Latest plan frozen at 2026-10-04T03:40:18.974165+00:00; code/tests were not audited in this delta.
reviews.decision: Advance the bounded Two Swarms, One World specification first. Preserve The Island No One Visits as the flagship mechanism, contingent on demonstrating decision-dependent observation rather than imposing avoidance in code.

interest.judgment: A compelling prospective question with a stronger causal story than ordinary misinformation spreading.
interest.why: A mistaken map could change inspection choices and thereby remove opportunities for correction. Distinguishing wrong judgments from missing corrective exposure would change how evidence-gathering systems are designed.
interest.novelty_boundary: Self-confirming learning, collective sensing, context effects and spatial demonstrations already appear in the proposal's cited work. Those sources were mostly scanned at abstract/introductory depth; no complete novelty search or new independent literature validation is supplied by this review. The possible contribution is an identified feedback mechanism and useful intervention, not a recognizable map or a persistent wrong label.

robustness.supported: The design correctly separates fixed evidence from adaptive observation, distinguishes retraction from deletion/reset, requires complete-world scoring and identifies pooled/deterministic baselines. The newly written PC-1 plan now specifies a 6×6 world, three same-evidence actors, eight history/communication/state trajectories, a complete final observation ledger, explicit retraction, fixed-denominator error bounds and byte-identical canonical reset inputs. These are plan properties, not validated execution.
robustness.unsupported: There is no evidence yet of amplification, a self-maintaining exploration trap, benefit from source-aware communication, model-specific susceptibility or recovery. Neither a selected animation nor an Earth-coordinate demonstration would establish these.
robustness.unit: An independently generated archipelago/world with its sensor and initial-exposure realization. History, communication and reset branches are paired within world; neighboring tiles and agents are dependent measurements.
robustness.independent_variation: None sampled yet. Vary world geometry, report ambiguity and exposure placement across held-out world families, rather than relabeling one coastline. Repeated identical requests estimate service variation, not environmental generalization.
robustness.assessment: Scientifically promising, but not execution-ready. The observation model, available actions, stopping horizon, memory contract, resource prices and primary estimand remain unspecified.

scenario_quality.size: PC-1 fixes 36 cells, three actors and twelve qualification worlds. That is sufficient for an instrument screen, not population inference; the proposed 1,044-call qualification ceiling is large for a simple complete-evidence task and should be staged.
scenario_quality.challenge: The final step supplies all 36 noiseless observations. This is an appropriate competence and history-persistence control but can reduce the task to copying a complete map. A null is valid. Claims about realistic exploration require the separate PC-2 observation-choice stage.
scenario_quality.complexity: PC-1 uses identical factual inputs for three actors, so it isolates communication rather than complementary sensing. Its three logical steps and strict-majority aggregation are deliberately small. PC-2 must add real observation choices without hardcoded avoidance.
scenario_quality.realism: A fictional text-survey task offers strong causal control and resembles evidence collection. It is not visual perception, geographic discovery or a demonstration of changed model weights.
scenario_quality.definition: PC-1 resolves the action/schema, cell coverage, UNKNOWN versus missing, world-level units and all-assignment error bounds. The primary interaction is in absolute between-history disagreement; accuracy must remain a separate outcome because convergence can be jointly wrong and disagreement can reflect service noise.

scenarios.name: Two Swarms, One World

Equal facts do not imply equal prompts, memory access or presentation order. Match initial information, sensor opportunities and total observation budget; allow realized observations to differ because they are the mediator. Randomize a forced audit observation to test whether restored exposure breaks the loop.

reviews.name: Quorum of Mirrors
reviews.evidence_class: Exploratory, unimplemented, unqualified proposal, DM-02. This is distinct from the existing adaptive-quorum experiment; its historical runs cannot be borrowed as Quorum of Mirrors results.
reviews.decision: Prioritize a small evidence-dependence benchmark with partial-lineage controls. The useful target is an intervention/resource tradeoff, not another demonstration that duplicated votes are dependent.

interest.judgment: A cleaner initial causal study than adaptive Phantom Coast, with practical value if it identifies when another observation beats another judgment.
interest.why: Source count, decision-maker count and communication can be manipulated separately. Explicit versus incomplete lineage tests when implementable deduplication works and when apparent consensus conceals dependence.
interest.novelty_boundary: The proposal itself identifies prior work on repeated evidence and correlated Jev judge errors. Reading remains limited; novelty is unestablished. Neither a hundred cloned calls, unanimous errors nor a renamed consensus task is a new scientific contribution.

robustness.supported: The revised design recognizes ancestry ground truth, task-difficulty confounding, confidence calibration, pooled baselines and separate observation/call budgets.
robustness.unsupported: No evidence yet that endorsements inflate confidence, partial lineage defeats a defense, a larger quorum helps, or Jev differs from other models. Typed valid outputs do not demonstrate calibrated decisions.
robustness.unit: An independently generated decision instance/world with a sampled evidence-ancestry graph. Judges, repeated calls and communication rounds are nested observations; branches using the same evidence graph are paired.
robustness.independent_variation: Not sampled yet. Different source IDs do not guarantee independent measurements: shared sensors, common causes and item difficulty can correlate distinct roots.
robustness.assessment: A strong sketch, not a protocol. Specify the generative dependence model, allowed lineage information, aggregation rules and budget estimands before claiming either independent sources or fair comparisons.

scenario_quality.size: A small fixed group can expose duplicate amplification. A hundred is a communication hook, not a necessary experimental scale or independent sample count.
scenario_quality.challenge: All-explicit source IDs may make deterministic deduplication trivial. Partial lineage adds meaningful ambiguity, but some ancestry configurations are observationally indistinguishable; impossible inference is an information limit, not a model defect.
scenario_quality.complexity: Use controlled noisy evidence and imperfect visible ancestry before adding large graphs. Separate exact copies, factual restatements and genuinely new measurements.
scenario_quality.realism: Mirrored reports and repeated endorsements resemble practical research/decision workflows. Grounded reliability cues are preferable to arbitrary crowd authority; real source dependence is rarely captured by identity alone.
scenario_quality.definition: Freeze fact-preserving paraphrases, lineage visibility, source reliability and how peer messages update state. Report calibrated error, agreement and raw dependence separately; an effective-sample-size approximation is not a literal count of independent minds.

scenarios.name: One Witness, a Hundred Votes
scenarios.assessment: Good flagship visualization and controlled dependence test; the generic phenomenon is already expected. The scientific opening is a defense that remains useful with incomplete ancestry at a known cost.
scenarios.improvement: Record true observation ancestry in the evaluator. Give actors explicit or partial lineage without truth labels; compare majority, implementable deduplication, calibrated accumulation and pooled evidence. Keep omniscient deduplication labeled an oracle.

scenarios.name: The Right Dissenter
scenarios.assessment: A useful stress test of an already formed quorum, not a reason to duplicate the independent dissent project. A designated truthful dissenter would leak the answer.
scenarios.improvement: Pair correct and incorrect fresh evidence with identical delivery budgets and reputation cues. Freeze the pre-injection checkpoint, include a silent/no-new-source comparator, and reuse RD-1 bounded checks as a declared intervention.

scenarios.name: The Next Observation
scenarios.assessment: Most direct operational payoff: buy another measurement or spend another model call. It cannot hold both source count and observation spending constant while changing evidence acquisition.
scenarios.improvement: Declare an equal-total-resource contrast with explicit prices and latency, separate from the fixed-information duplication contrast. Report a cost-sensitivity frontier; avoid presenting it as a general optimal swarm-size study.

scenarios.name: The Crowd That Learns to Agree
scenarios.assessment: Useful diagnostic within the flagship. Faster agreement is not automatically harmful; convergence can reflect valid evidence aggregation.
scenarios.improvement: Plot agreement, correctness and calibration jointly at every scheduled round, including failures and abstentions. Stratify shared errors by preregistered task difficulty and report joint failure patterns.

interest.judgment: The resilience question is worthwhile; the present model task has limited research depth.
interest.why: Local mistakes can produce globally valid but inefficient systems. That distinction is useful. Here the controller supplies path certificates, loop exclusion and synchronization, while the model mostly chooses the smallest displayed integer.
interest.novelty_boundary: This is neither learned NCA regeneration nor evidence of emergent cooperation. Novelty would require a distinct, identified result about error structure, recovery or information loss; visual resemblance and 200 identities are insufficient.

robustness.supported: All 486 frames reconstruct exactly. Algorithm ends 100% shortest; Qwen/hybrid end 6.5% shortest despite 100% certificate validity. Hybrid gives no final endpoint benefit; its two distinct overrides do not select a minimum.
robustness.unsupported: General resilience, diversity advantage, packet-delivery recovery, or superiority of 4-round model recovery over 18-round algorithm recovery.
robustness.unit: A complete map-and-damage world, with paired conditions.
robustness.independent_variation: One hard-coded map, one damage location/time, fixed head placement; qualification fixtures were adapted. Six arms are not six independent scenarios.
robustness.assessment: Strong trace integrity and candid limitations; weak identification beyond this implementation. Model detours lower damage exposure, so recovery speeds compare differently damaged initial route systems.

scenario_quality.size: 200 cells/199 decision makers is enough to expose propagation; it adds no replication. Increase map diversity before population.
scenario_quality.challenge: Numerically trivial local task with a meaningful distributed consistency problem; difficulty comes primarily from model arithmetic errors and stale state.
scenario_quality.complexity: Two partitions, one closed door and one erased patch; two damage mechanisms are bundled. No congestion, capacity, deadlines or changing costs.
scenario_quality.realism: Useful routing abstraction, weak evacuation model: no moving packets or competing traffic. Shared stateless model calls are controller-managed identities.
scenario_quality.definition: Certificate scoring is precise; current next-hop forwarding is a different outcome. Memory erasure clears route state, not the decision cache.

scenarios.improvement: Freeze disjoint decision fixtures spanning candidate counts, near ties and route lengths; qualify the interface separately from scientific endpoints.

reviews.name: Avalon Swarm: evidence circulation, audit and repair
reviews.evidence_class: Scripted engineering benchmark: 15 scale worlds, 15 recovery worlds and 15 consensus-mechanics worlds; no LLM evidence.
reviews.decision: Advance a narrow memory-repair mechanism at 100 agents. Defer population expansion and paid agents until useful evidence and consensus controls discriminate.

interest.judgment: Potentially strong, provided verified correction improves decisions beyond mechanically suppressing claims.
interest.why: Audit availability and downstream repair are separated, making persistent misinformation testable. Team proposals and mission consequences provide task utility beyond agreement.
interest.novelty_boundary: This is an independent Avalon-inspired game, not AvalonBench comparability or autonomous deception detection. Existing scripted repair demonstrates an implemented rule, not learned institutional behavior.

robustness.supported: All 45 outcomes/source identities validate; 15 event chains verify. Repair reduces audited-contradiction exposures 79.6→54.8 on average. Later mission success rises 37.3%→38.0%, exactly one additional mission across five paired seeds; council wins are unchanged.
robustness.unsupported: Reliable repair efficacy, scaling intelligence, LLM throughput, autonomous malicious-agent detection or universal swarm collapse.
robustness.unit: Complete connected world; councils communicate and are not independent replicates.
robustness.independent_variation: Five paired seeds for recovery at 100 agents; one seed per size/topology for each scale sweep.
robustness.assessment: Clear scoring and reproducible mechanics; limited behavioral diversity. Counts of repeated messages inflate apparent evidence volume without adding independent information.

scenario_quality.size: 100–2, 000 agents means 10–200 fixed ten-member councils. LargerN replicates a local game more than it increases individual reasoning complexity.
scenario_quality.challenge: Hidden roles and coupled evidence create genuine uncertainty, but weak heuristics, mandatory sabotage and random assassination dominate current difficulty.
scenario_quality.complexity: Five missions, bounded messages/memory and a ring are tractable. Each target has one noisy original signal; copying is not corroboration.
scenario_quality.realism: Useful controlled misinformation abstraction. Perfect environment audits, numeric claims and programmed repair are far from contested institutional evidence.
scenario_quality.definition: Game rules are explicit and differ openly from standard Avalon. Consensus starts before knowledge acquisition, so failure can mean never learning rather than losing established knowledge.

scenarios.improvement: Measure unaudited decisions and retained useful evidence; isolate memory-capacity effects and split random streams by phase so pruning cannot change unrelated proposal randomness.

reviews.name: Optimal swarm size: a deployable conditional launch policy
reviews.evidence_class: Detailed prospective design only. No implemented harness, validated task generator, qualification, model episode, or sizing result is established by these documents.
reviews.decision: Develop the task contracts and a smaller identifying pilot. Defer the proposed 2,512-episode core/transfer programme and 1,280-episode optional extension until useful size-dependent heterogeneity exists and the runtime is measurable.

interest.judgment: Scientifically worthwhile and operationally clear, with unusually careful prospective controls.
interest.why: A launch rule that increases verified success under an actual deadline and aggregate budget is useful; charging selection, coordination, retrieval, retries and cancellation makes the question substantially more meaningful than a best-looking N sweep.
interest.novelty_boundary: Task- and architecture-dependent scaling is already acknowledged in the design. The proposed contribution is a deployable rule evaluated on fresh executions with charged overhead, not discovery of a universal optimum. Novelty remains unestablished pending the focused methods comparison.

robustness.supported: The draft specifies a coherent estimand, independent-root splits, intention-to-treat failures, hidden evaluators, aggregate resource accounting, paired comparisons and fresh policy evaluation. These are design strengths, not demonstrated harness properties.
robustness.unsupported: No evidence yet supports an optimal size, reliable five-point near-optimality, a learned selector, physical-memory effects, or cross-domain transfer. One locked transfer family supports one-family transfer only.
robustness.unit: An independently generated task root; repeated model samples, paraphrases, sizes and profiles remain nested or paired within that root.
robustness.independent_variation: Root semantics and dependencies, plus independent model sampling. Two development families and one transfer family do not create a broad population of independent task domains.
robustness.assessment: Four fit and four validation roots per structural cell cannot establish fine conditional boundaries. The documents candidly flag this. Choose complexity and interval interpretation accordingly; do not let 2,512 correlated episodes imply strong precision. Simultaneous uncertainty must govern the smallest-within-epsilon decision.

scenario_quality.size: N=1,2,4,8,16 counts addressable stateful contexts including the coordinator; four runnable slots in P0 make N>4 a queue/context-capacity intervention as well as a roster intervention. This is legitimate but must be interpreted explicitly.
scenario_quality.challenge: The arithmetic dossier and clamp repair are contract illustrations, not evidence of research-grade difficulty. Establish non-ceiling correctness and a genuine serial/parallel tradeoff before the response map.
scenario_quality.complexity: Vary dependency width/depth while matching atomic work, output count and evaluator burden. The roster-aware model also constructs a plan, so primary effects concern the whole protocol, including changed decomposition quality.
scenario_quality.realism: Repository repair offers practical task structure; synthetic dossiers and simulated incidents offer control. None yet captures long-running deployment, evolving requirements, human escalation or uncontrolled services, which should remain outside the initial claim.
scenario_quality.definition: Exact artifact contracts, equivalent repair sequences and accepted alternative citation proofs are strong. Pin all currently open actor-turn, truncation, initialization and integration-reserve values before implementation.

scenarios.assessment: The 16 N=1 screening episodes and 64 larger-roster episodes intentionally use different caps; they cannot estimate a size effect. Success-conditioned pooled cost/time quantiles select an operating regime rather than a production SLA.
scenarios.improvement: Check cap-hit and solvability distributions by family/structure before freezing the core. Separate marginal cost/time quantiles do not guarantee joint feasibility. Preserve screening failures and stop when a cell is trivial or impossible.

scenarios.improvement: Use matched multistep provenance problems with plausible distractors and alternative valid proofs. Keep distractor load fixed initially; vary dependency structure, not every difficulty dimension simultaneously.

scenarios.name: Repository repair: independent defects versus interface chains
scenarios.assessment: A useful second family with real integration costs. Isolated copies and deterministic merging prevent uncontrolled filesystem races, but this is a particular coordination protocol; merge conflicts may dominate the apparent size effect.
scenarios.improvement: Match defect count and hidden-test burden; report planning, patch correctness and integration failures separately. Include meaningful interface dependencies rather than many independent one-line fixes.

scenarios.name: Incident triage: locked transfer
scenarios.assessment: Stateful observations, safety constraints and equivalent repair sequences are a stronger transfer test than renamed arithmetic. A task contract exists, but no reviewed held-out fixture yet demonstrates complexity or realizability.
scenarios.improvement: Validate the simulator and evaluator with separate development fixtures. Freeze transfer generators and selector features before revealing transfer outcomes; report the narrow family-transfer boundary.

scenarios.name: Core P0/P1/P2/P3 and optional M1/M2/M3/H1
scenarios.assessment: Baseline, half deadline, half budget and one runnable slot are interpretable one-axis contrasts. Reduced context, no ledger, reduced physical memory and eight slots are distinct extensions; no-ledger changes communication architecture.
scenarios.improvement: Initially prioritize N-by-dependency; add N-by-deadline or N-by-service-capacity only when the first pilot identifies a mechanism. Defer physical-memory claims until local measurement is available, and label ledger removal a protocol change.

scenarios.name: Fresh locked selector evaluation
scenarios.assessment: Charging selection and keeping the transfer size map sealed are excellent protections against hindsight. A global best fixed N is insufficient by itself to establish the value of task-conditioned sizing.
scenarios.improvement: Compare against a development-frozen resource-profile-only size rule, or explicitly make this an ablation of the existing heuristic. This distinguishes useful task features from simply responding to a tighter deadline or fewer slots.

controls.retain: N=1 with the same tools and sequential work interface; equal retrievable evidence union; aggregate budgets; coordinator included in N; hidden evaluator; all failures retained; paired roots; fresh policy runs; charged initialization/selection; source and context receipts.
controls.missing: A resource-only selector comparison for incremental task-feature value, and a separate deterministic scheduling fixture with a known public work graph to distinguish scheduler overhead from model decomposition errors. The latter is harness validation, not an oracle-assisted primary arm.
controls.confounds: Roster-dependent plans, N-by-service contention, aggregate context capacity and integration conflicts are combined in the operational effect. External API load and version changes require randomized blocked execution; logical concurrency is not a physical-hardware measurement.

reviews.evidence_class: Completed exploratory model experiment; traces independently recomputed, without independent laboratory replication.
reviews.decision: Retain as an instrument and boundary on stronger claims. Redirect scientific effort to selective continuity.

interest.judgment: Modest scientific interest; good engineering feasibility evidence.
interest.why: Procedure accuracy and arbitrary phrase retention are separated, and qualification failures preserved. However, founders receive the answer; copying a short record solves the task.
interest.novelty_boundary: This demonstrates neither spontaneous acquisition nor a swarm advantage. Memory usefulness, replacement and multigenerational transmission alone establish no novelty.

robustness.supported: All 36 S1 trajectories completed. Both and notes each achieved 100% versus 52.08% without inheritance; both-minus-neither was +47.92 percentage points. All 216 main-study frames reconcile with recorded requests/responses. Mentoring alone averaged 91.67%; adding it to notes produced no observed task gain.
robustness.unsupported: Generalization, emergence, beneficial turnover, mentoring superiority, cumulative improvement and identity preservation. The bootstrap interval is correctly computed but poorly calibrated by two worlds per scenario.
robustness.unit: Six paired world IDs; agents, steps and cases are repeated measurements.
robustness.independent_variation: One model snapshot and two seeds per scenario, largely counterbalancing two mappings. There are only two substantive task mechanisms because seed bank and repair dock share XOR structure.
robustness.assessment: The numerical result is reproducible; inference is narrow. More traces from this construction would add precision without separating explanations.

scenario_quality.size: Three agents are sufficient to test a handoff instrument; four binary cases per step are insufficient for structural transfer.
scenario_quality.challenge: Notes and verbatim arms are at ceiling; the correct rule is short and supplied.
scenario_quality.complexity: Hard-coded majority aggregation of independent answers provides little need for coordination or complementary roles.
scenario_quality.realism: Recognizable stories wrap highly artificial computations. The arbitrary receipt phrase has no operational consequence.
scenario_quality.definition: Actions and scoring are clear. Rename culture/identity outcomes to procedure/phrase retention.

scenarios.assessment: A valid memory-transmission positive control. Every solve repeats the four possible binary inputs; new IDs do not create new reasoning problems.
scenarios.improvement: Keep as a cheap regression fixture; use acquired multistep procedures and withheld combinations in the next scientific task.

scenarios.improvement: Vary duplicate concentration, conflicting root reports and incomplete provenance separately; retain an exact source-aware oracle.

scenarios.name: Repair dock
scenarios.assessment: Measures obeying an explicit reversal bulletin despite old memory. It does not measure detecting change or selectively revising a practice.
scenarios.improvement: Replace the full new mapping with observations that identify one changed component while another remains valid.

reviews.name: Healing Helping Hands: extraction and evidence-repair pilots
reviews.evidence_class: Completed deterministic mechanism experiments plus semantic model qualification and a successful Jev reference pilot; requested Qwen/heterogeneous arms remain unexecuted.
reviews.decision: Retain as an audited systems demonstration. Advance toward constrained, error-bearing repair; increasing agent count is unnecessary.

interest.judgment: Useful mechanistic separation, but the positive withdrawal result is largely expected from programmed tombstone dissemination.
interest.why: Separating extraction, provenance, invalidation and memory repair makes failures diagnosable. The next interesting result is where repair fails or creates costs.
interest.novelty_boundary: Trusted invalidation propagation is not a newly learned swarm capability. Perfect template classification followed by deterministic set exchange cannot establish heterogeneous reasoning or real-paper evidence quality.

robustness.supported: Pilot03 contains all 180 assignments: 72 complete and 108 explicitly not-run. All 72 completed worlds replay exactly, including 1,728 frames and event snapshots. Jev matched exact labels on all 600 pilot reports after fresh 60/60 qualification. Combined-event notice propagation reduced integrated atlas error by 28.095 percentage points on average, range 25.000–30.357 across three seeds.
robustness.unsupported: Qwen competence, attachment benefit, heterogeneous-swarm benefit, robustness to realistic extraction errors, forged withdrawals or autonomous scientific judgment.
robustness.unit: Three corpus seeds; policy/event branches share extraction tapes. Nodes, rounds, votes and model/exact duplicates are dependent.
robustness.independent_variation: Three small corpora and narrow qualification phrases. Jev-exact equality means 72 trajectories are not 72 independent semantic realizations.
robustness.assessment: Strong replay/provenance evidence for this mechanism, weak evidence for broader capability. Earlier scattered erasure was ineffective after redundant spreading; pilot03 repairs manipulation validity but damage still recovers quickly. A post-hoc always-UNCERTAIN predictor scores 75%, 65%, 50% on final combined worlds, versus evidence-only 65%, 65%, 70%; these values independently reconcile. Class imbalance makes accuracy alone misleading.

scenario_quality.size: 200 scouts look substantial, but they serve 20 claims with ten redundant curators each; there are 100 source roots and two copies per root.
scenario_quality.challenge: Unlimited deterministic exchange and trusted notices make long-run convergence easy. The contiguous erasure creates measurable damage, but first-exchange atlas accuracy is already 95%.
scenario_quality.complexity: Each scout makes one semantic call, then follows programmed dynamics for 24 rounds; no repeated deliberation, active reading or costly source selection.
scenario_quality.realism: Fictional reports omit evidence strength, methods and uncertain withdrawals. Gold means surviving-source consensus, not scientific truth.
scenario_quality.definition: Policies and paired counterfactuals are clear. Report event-before-exchange and recovery indexing separately: recovery_rounds=0 can mean the first exchange already crosses the threshold, not zero repair work.

scenarios.name: No event
scenarios.assessment: Necessary competence/convergence baseline and cost control; it is not evidence of healing.
scenarios.improvement: Retain under every resource limit; expose communication cost and false confidence alongside accuracy.

reviews.name: Heterogeneous swarms: five prospective mechanism studies (HX-02, HX-01, HX-03, HX-05, HX-09)
reviews.evidence_class: Prospective design sketches only. Reviewed pinned README.md and DESIGNS.md at dmarzzz/swarm-lab f027940fcb5b892057e65306f8e7550456ed2945; no experimental results or qualified model configurations accompany these two documents.
reviews.decision: Keep the staged programme, but run one qualified mechanism study first. HX-02 is a practical first candidate; HX-03 has the clearest scientific question about information dependence. HX-01 and HX-09 first need inexpensive control/queue demonstrations; merge HX-05 with recovery work unless it adds an identifiable response-diversity mechanism. None currently supports an effectiveness or novelty claim.

interest.judgment: Editorial assessment: Scientifically promising questions with unusually sensible baseline and stopping language for early sketches; the interest lies in mechanisms, not mixing vendor names.
interest.why: The designs separate allocation, stale plans, correlated errors, reserve exposure and rejection feedback. Typed decision interfaces can make those mechanisms measurable, especially when generated plans and reports are unreliable.
interest.novelty_boundary: Adaptive allocation, multirate control, ensemble complementarity, redundancy and queue admission are established ideas, as the document recognizes. The 85–92 shortlist scores express owner preferences, not evidence or scientific quality. A frontier claim needs a new failure regime or transferable mechanism beyond ordinary code and capability-matched homogeneous teams; the stated literature scan is not yet a completed methods-level novelty assessment.

robustness.supported: The protocol sketches correctly propose independent worlds, paired disturbances, development/test separation, preserved failed qualifications, objective evaluators, realized resource reporting and simple-rule kill criteria. They explicitly avoid treating provider identity as immutable or seeds as new task families.
robustness.unsupported: No model has demonstrated the required stage capabilities here; no task generator, frozen difficulty distribution, semantic adapter validation, variance estimate, effect estimate or sample-size justification is supplied. These are readiness gaps, not negative results.
robustness.unit: An independently generated task world or graph, with all decisions, agents and repeated calls nested within it. Paired arm outcomes share a world; repeating a seed or provider call is not another task population.
robustness.independent_variation: Vary graph structure, task content, capability requirements and exogenous shocks across worlds. Block by family and development-calibrated difficulty. Repeated model realizations can estimate within-world variability; a second family tests transfer only after the first mechanism is established.
robustness.assessment: The suggested 12 development worlds per family is a feasibility starting point, not an adequacy threshold. Pilot variation, rare-failure frequency and precision around a prespecified useful-effect margin should determine later allocation. Test families and disturbance regimes must be frozen before confirmatory evaluation.

scenario_quality.size: No fixed graph or swarm size is scientifically required yet. A small graph can identify the mechanism if it has genuine dependencies, alternative assignments and constrained resources. Size should increase only when pilots show ceiling effects or missing congestion/propagation, and independent-world count should follow precision planning rather than node count.
scenario_quality.challenge: Calibrate away both trivial success and capability-floor failure. Demonstrate stage-specific competence, useful specialization crossovers and a solvable recovery path. Difficulty must arise from relevant dependencies, timing or information uncertainty, not gratuitous prompt length or instructions that models cannot follow.
scenario_quality.complexity: The shared interface is suitably lean. Each design should initially manipulate its named mechanism with a small fixed architecture. Topology, model combinations, memory and workload should not all change simultaneously; a complete factorial across the programme would waste budget.
scenario_quality.realism: Synthetic worlds offer exact truth and interventions but presently assume outages, delays, erroneous reports and service costs. These can establish conditional mechanism results. Later transfer should use measured latency/error distributions and a second task family; synthetic family-correlated outages alone cannot establish real provider resilience.
scenario_quality.definition: Prospective status and launch gates are clear. Remaining specification work includes executable task success, workload sampling, informative observations, adaptation overhead, evaluator independence, exact initial capability and action opportunities. Role names, model labels and actual capabilities need separate fields and displays.

scenarios.name: HX-02 — Adaptive division of labor after a capability shock
scenarios.assessment: A good first study if workers demonstrably differ in stage competence and reassignment can change outcomes. Tool withdrawal supplies an interpretable capability intervention; injected error-distribution changes are useful simulations but not observations about natural model deterioration. B versus the tuned progress rule is the right primary comparison. Honest progress alone tests ordinary allocation, while the stated novelty specifically concerns stale or unreliable reports.
scenarios.improvement: Freeze a development capability matrix, graph bottlenecks, shock severity and recovery opportunity; include matched no-shock worlds to expose switching overhead. Give allocators identical observable histories and charge context transfer, compilation and reassignment time. Retain same-model differentiated-tool teams to separate role/capability partitioning from model diversity. After qualification, make one prespecified stale-report contrast mandatory if claiming unreliable-progress novelty; misleading-report stress and additional shock types can follow.

scenarios.name: HX-01 — Reflexes and deliberation
scenarios.assessment: The version/expiry intervention is well defined and practically useful, but may primarily rediscover validity checking and delay compensation. Its protection-plus-fallback arm bundles two mechanisms. Counting feasible actions can reward harmless low-value actions, so apparent protection need not improve delivered service. A useful world needs demands and route changes where stale plans matter and safe fallback has a measurable opportunity cost.
scenarios.improvement: Use objectively served demand or completed routing work by deadline, with constraint violations reported separately, or define a useful-action criterion that excludes no-ops. Match state, memory and action opportunities. First compare the full protection policy against unprotected control; add one diagnostic checks-only/fallback-only ablation if claiming which component works. Freeze one delay relative to environmental change timescale; the delay-by-refresh map is later exploration. Report exogenous injected delay separately from actual model latency.

scenarios.name: HX-03 — Diversity as a firebreak
scenarios.assessment: The most compelling conceptual question is whether evidence dependence changes the value of a different-model monitor. The proposed two-by-two contrast is appropriate, but a difference-in-differences alone does not isolate error covariance: monitor competence, marginal evidence quality and response thresholds can also interact with evidence sharing. Synthetic false reports must be difficult enough to require judgment while some correct minority reports remain worth preserving.
scenarios.improvement: Hold marginal sensor quality, observation budget, topology and permissible actions fixed while randomizing whether sources are shared or independent. Measure sensitivity/specificity and conditional co-failure on held-out items and disclose residual capability imbalance; family labels are not independence measurements. Include useful correct commitments and false quarantine alongside false commitments to defeat universal abstention. Keep the existing deterministic-check and extra-solving controls. Placement/topology stress comes later; monitor composition by evidence dependence is the mandatory interaction.

scenarios.name: HX-05 — Diverse reserves for recovery
scenarios.assessment: The insurance tradeoff is interesting, but this overlaps existing recovery studies and risks constructing the answer through a family-targeted outage. Equal damage and identical dependency events answer different questions: equal lost capacity estimates recovery conditional on damage, whereas the same outage may legitimately damage diversified teams less. These should not be silently mixed. Local surviving memory makes state restoration a substantive additional mechanism.
scenarios.improvement: Declare the primary estimand as conditional recovery or total insurance value. For the former, match lost qualified capacity and report coverage restoration; for the latter, use identical exogenous dependency events and count exposure reduction as part of the policy. Charge idle capacity, model loading, storage and checkpoint availability, include clean opportunity-cost worlds, and forbid reserves from receiving unavailable state. Independently parameterize family exposure and task competence. Real shared-provider resilience requires observed dependencies, not only simulated family labels.

scenarios.name: HX-09 — Verification queues and the cost of saying no
scenarios.assessment: A useful operations study if revisions feed back into the queue and verification has real semantic errors. Pure replay can isolate this feedback but cannot establish native-model error rates. The planned backpressure-plus-reserved-budget treatment is a policy package, so a win cannot yet be attributed to admission alone. Near-capacity must refer to measured service capacity, not a nominal proposal rate.
scenarios.improvement: Freeze an assigned workload with task difficulty and deadlines; count dropped, rejected and unfinished tasks in that denominator. Measure service-time tails, proposal validity and retry transitions, then set offered load relative to calibrated capacity. reviews.evidence_class: Prospective hypotheses only. Bounded late read of five local documents frozen 2026-10-04T03:23:55.191217+00:00 at a515aed7a85a6387564a8fe883586e87d254a794, with no uncommitted changes in that directory. The task was active; later changes are outside this cutoff. No new experimental results.
reviews.decision: In this reviewer’s editorial judgment, this revision substantially improves conceptual interest and supersedes the older shortlist as the author’s recommended research focus. Retain all eight as questions, prioritize methods review of HX-31 and HX-32, and use HX-37 as a comparatively direct first mechanism pilot. Do not mistake a compelling biological label for established novelty or a measured evolutionary transition.

interest.judgment: Editorial assessment: Stronger scientific agenda than the operational HX shortlist: each leading idea proposes a causal intervention on dependence, compatibility, inherited environment or artifact supply.
interest.why: Helper removal/rescue, reciprocal partner swaps, habitat transplants and translated module recombination are informative even when the biological analogy fails. The new designs identify nulls worth publishing and explicitly separate fixed base models from mutable policies.
interest.novelty_boundary: The documents acknowledge close predecessors and abstract-level reading limits. This pass assesses the new designs, not an independently completed novelty search. Co-inheritance selected by a harness, information reuse and model-family differences alone do not demonstrate new levels of individuality, biological speciation or ecological coexistence.

robustness.supported: Strong prospective controls: fixed model weights, finite copying, population caps, held-out evaluation, retained failed lineages, counterbalanced initial capabilities, homogeneous comparators, rescue tests and charged overhead.
robustness.unsupported: No capability-loss mechanism, successful adaptation, stable pair dependence, habitat feedback, procedural incompatibility or consumer niche has yet been observed. Exact selection, mutation, inheritance and information-access rules remain unspecified.
robustness.unit: Independent adapted population, pair lineage, island or built habitat according to the study. Frozen descendants can have independent evaluation episodes conditional on that ancestor, but those episodes do not add independent adaptation histories.
robustness.independent_variation: Replicate independent starting lineages and construction histories; pair held-out tasks across frozen descendants. Within-lineage generations and offspring are dependent. Use multiple independent donor artifact pools for salvage transfer.
robustness.assessment: Specify a primary joint signature or contrast and a useful-effect margin before confirmation. Size pilots by feasibility and variance of independent lineages; generations, islands, task families and model realizations answer different uncertainty questions. There is no justified universal minimum population size.

scenario_quality.size: Small finite populations are appropriate for the first interventions. They must support alternative helpers, partner swaps or reciprocal habitats as relevant. Sustained coexistence needs longitudinal resource-share evidence and invasion tests; one successful trajectory cannot substitute for that stronger claim.
scenario_quality.challenge: Choose tasks with verified subskills and useful intermediate artifacts. Avoid both trivial answer copying and models incapable of solo/component tasks. Capability loss must change executable ability, not merely delete a label while the base model can still perform the operation.
scenario_quality.complexity: The strongest designs have several stages. Separate qualification, bounded adaptation, frozen evaluation and one causal intervention; add population feedback only after the simpler interaction is established. A full cross-product of models, selection rules and environments is unnecessary.
scenario_quality.realism: Compute, context, tool access and interface costs can ground the analogies. Unused skill files may have no maintenance cost; text is non-rival; the harness controls reproduction. Artificial cost schedules and selection incentives support conditional simulations, not direct claims about naturally evolving agent ecologies.
scenario_quality.definition: The documents are clear about prospective status and operational analogy. They now need an exact mutable representation, allowed mutation/copy operations, local versus group selection objective, exposure history, resource price, intervention semantics and evaluator-visible versus actor-visible labels.

scenarios.name: HX-31 — Black Queen capability loss
scenarios.assessment: Most conceptually compelling if deletion saves an actual recurring cost and creates experimentally verified dependence. The pruning/public-access crossing and helper-rescue tests are strong. Selecting policies by group reward could intentionally engineer efficient division of labor, which is a narrower result than individual-level selection causing dependence.
scenarios.improvement: Declare whose utility controls selection; verify capability loss using matched solo tests and actual denied tool access. Measure retained-skill context/tool overhead and include the proposed zero-cost and optimized fixed-specialist controls. Require selective helper withdrawal, matched ordinary removal and capability-equivalent rescue. Treat the four-part signature as joint evidence rather than selecting its most favorable component.

scenarios.name: HX-32 — Symbiotic pairs and escape from lock-in
scenarios.assessment: Partner-specific interface adaptation is valuable research on upgrade fragility. Pair copying imposed by the harness establishes an experimental inheritance rule, not emergence of a higher-level individual. A Jev selector may never solve the complete generative task alone, making whole-task solo failure uninformative.
scenarios.improvement: Qualify each component on its own legitimate task and start with an interoperable, replaceable partner. Evaluate a reciprocal partner matrix to separate component quality from compatibility. Prespecify task shift and normalization semantics, charge translation calls and test its competence. First show pair-specific interaction; adaptation/escape is the next stage, and any transition claim needs additional evidence beyond enforced joint copying.

scenarios.name: HX-33 — Habitat inheritance and model-family feedback
scenarios.assessment: Reciprocal builder/newcomer effects improve substantially on generic persistent-memory studies. A family interaction can still reflect interface familiarity or training-style overlap; it is not necessarily a self-reinforcing population process. Equal-information controls and fixed-composition arms are therefore essential.
scenarios.improvement: Freeze independent builder habitats, use held-out tasks disjoint from stored complete solutions, and audit actual retrieval/context exposure. Compare portable normalized artifacts without giving one model extra evidence. Establish the relative-performance interaction before applying the fixed recruitment rule. Report recruitment as a consequence under that rule; test reintroduction from rarity before claiming exclusion or stable feedback.

scenarios.name: HX-35 — Cultural speciation through procedural incompatibility
scenarios.assessment: Procedural hybrid failure after translation is interesting, but translator failure cannot by itself prove deep incompatibility. Arbitrary shuffled modules may already be broken, weakening the proposed reference distribution. Migration can prevent fragmentation through ordinary information transfer without any speciation mechanism.
scenarios.improvement: Demonstrate initial cross-island compatibility and test translators on known alignable procedures. Use linkage-breaking controls that preserve valid component interfaces and evaluate native/hybrid matrices at fixed adaptation milestones. Report residual incompatibility under tested translators, not impossibility of translation. Freeze migration doses and match communication cost; broader migration curves follow the first credible co-adaptation interaction.

scenarios.name: HX-37 — Cross-feeding on failed artifacts
scenarios.assessment: The clearest bounded first pilot. A failed complete attempt can contain valuable subresults, but oracle selection of verified useful fragments can supply an uncharged verifier or leak evaluator knowledge. A one-shot salvage gain is weaker than a consumer earning a persistent resource niche.
scenarios.improvement: Define an actor-available fragment selection procedure, charge validation/filtering, and hide evaluator-only validity labels. Freeze donor attempts before exposure assignment. Compare consumer transformation with identical-donor continuation, direct reuse and fresh attempts at equal total cost. Establish useful salvage first; then test withdrawal/rescue and resource-share dynamics under a fixed general allocation rule without consumer quotas.

scenarios.name: HX-34 — Selfish skills (reserve question)
scenarios.assessment: Separating skill spread from host task value is interesting; copying according to adoption mechanically rewards spread, so prevalence alone is tautological evidence. Benign format/readability differences can mimic a replication advantage.
scenarios.improvement: Measure transmission choices under matched exposure before applying selection, compare independently verified host utility, and keep copy opportunities and length controlled. Restrict claims to a replication–utility conflict under the declared rule; preserve the benign scope.

scenarios.name: HX-36 — Kill the winner (reserve question)
scenarios.assessment: Useful minority persistence under behavior-targeted pressure is plausible, but a challenge generator can manufacture whichever niche it targets. Positive minority share over a short run is not stable coexistence.
scenarios.improvement: Freeze an independent utility evaluation set, target behavioral strategy rather than provider, and match challenge difficulty. Test rare-policy growth across starting frequencies and retain no-feedback/random-challenge controls. Report finite-horizon coexistence under the chosen environment before any broader ecological claim.

scenarios.name: HX-38 — Swarm embryos (close alternate)
scenarios.assessment: Transient induction followed by repair could expose organizational memory, but persistent prompt text or shared labels can trivially preserve apparent roles. Symmetry breaking requires initially exchangeable opportunities, which model heterogeneity can violate.
scenarios.improvement: Cross-foster and blind names, record capabilities separately from emergent functions, and include same-model initial populations. Cross erasure of individual history and shared artifacts without changing task access. Validate role labels against task contributions and test actual recovery after turnover; persistence alone is insufficient.

retain: Homogeneous specialists, deterministic typed gate, fixed optimized specialization, held-out tasks, independent truth and exact intervention/rescue traces.
